findings.finding: The scheduled 2026 guidance re-base (promised in the H1 release once CdI completed) will probably cut 2026 capex, because the majority of the USD 55m guide was MaBoMo Phase 2 drilling that the rig loss has deferred, while CdI lifts pro forma production to about 20k boepd. That is a near-term FCF positive set against a 2027 Dussafu growth delay the market already absorbed (-6.3% on 26 Oct, BW Energy's guidance cut on 29 Oct).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean guidance-change result day: Q1 2026 (guide reiterated) -1.14%, Q3 2025 +0.25%, H1 2026 (with the CdI deal) +0.17%; the rig-loss day was -6.34% on 26 Oct with Brent flat
findings.why_not_priced: The capex consequence has not been quantified by Panoro. Its 4 Nov update says only it is 'assessing the impact ... on its future outlook', and BW Energy suspended rather than restated capex. If the market had priced a lower-capex, higher-FCF 2026, the stock would not sit at 30.3, below where it traded before the rig loss (33.9 on 23 Oct), while Brent is back near 94. But that gap is mostly oil (Brent 117 to 94), so this is inference and kept small.
findings.independence: BW Energy (operator, 73.5%) suspended 2026 capex guidance on 29 Oct: https://www.worldoil.com/news/2026/10/29/bw-energy-suspends-2026-capex-guidance-as-prospector-5-loss-delays-mabomo-phase-2-drilling-offshore-gabon/ ; the H1 commitment to update guidance: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680244

findings.finding: The Q3 cash distribution is boxed in by the stated 2026 capacity of USD 21.6m (~NOK 205m), with NOK 150m already paid. That leaves about NOK 55m, so the most likely outcome is another NOK 50m (~NOK 0.36/share, ~1.2% quarterly yield), with no room for an increase and a small risk the board pauses after the rig incident.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distributions have been announced with results each quarter (NOK 80m at Q3 2025, then NOK 50m in each 2026 quarter); the results-day moves were +0.25%, -1.14% and +0.17%, i.e. the in-line distribution did not move the stock
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it lands inside what the company guided (capacity and quarterly cadence), so it is sized near 0. The residual is the asymmetry: holders anchored on a record October lifting may hope for more, and the stated capacity does not allow it.
findings.independence: Q1 release states the same capacity and the 'prudent ... quarterly basis' wording: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=674065

findings.finding: Full-year pro forma liftings guidance of 5.1-5.5m bbl needs about 1.5-1.9m bbl lifted in Nov-Dec after 2.86m through 9M plus 0.715m in October, against about 2.0m bbl available (1.17m inventory plus ~1.5m Q4 oil production less October). That is tight enough that a cargo could slip into 2027 and the liftings guide be trimmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed liftings-guidance change in the sampled history; lifting timing drove the Q1 2026 loss (USD -43.3m) and that day moved -1.14%
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is mine, not the company's. Its 4 Nov update reports 9M liftings 'in line' and does not restate the full-year range, so nobody has published the Nov-Dec requirement. It is a timing item (cash moves to January), so even if confirmed the market likely looks through it; sized small.
